column1: # kind|MM-DD|year|Greek name|English name|English biography   (English versions of the short biographies in data/bios; kind is always bio)

bio|07-03|1962|Τομ Κρουζ|Tom Cruise|Tom Cruise is an American actor and producer. He became known through "Top Gun" and starred in the "Mission: Impossible" film series, in which he often performs the dangerous scenes himself.

bio|07-03|1971|Τζούλιαν Ασάνζ|Julian Assange|Julian Assange was born in Australia and founded the WikiLeaks website, which published confidential government documents. He spent years in the Ecuadorian embassy in London, and his case drew international attention to the public debate on press freedom.

bio|07-03|1971|Τζιμ Μόρισον|Jim Morrison|Jim Morrison was the singer and lyricist of the American band The Doors. He was known for his stage presence and his poetic writing. He died in Paris in 1971, at the age of 27.

bio|07-03|1987|Σεμπάστιαν Φέτελ|Sebastian Vettel|Sebastian Vettel is a German racing driver. He won four consecutive Formula One world championships with Red Bull, from 2010 to 2013, and later raced for Ferrari.

bio|07-04|1546|Μουράτ Γ΄|Murad III|Murad III was Ottoman sultan from 1574 to 1595. During his reign the empire fought with the Persians and the Habsburgs, and the influence of the harem on politics increased.

bio|07-04|1804|Νάθανιελ Χόθορν|Nathaniel Hawthorne|Nathaniel Hawthorne was an American writer from Salem, Massachusetts. He wrote the novel "The Scarlet Letter" and short stories that examine guilt and morality in Puritan society.

bio|07-04|1807|Τζουζέπε Γκαριμπάλντι|Giuseppe Garibaldi|Giuseppe Garibaldi was an Italian soldier and patriot. He led the Expedition of the Redshirts in 1860 in Sicily and Naples and contributed to the unification of Italy. He also fought in South America.

bio|07-04|1826|Τόμας Τζέφερσον|Thomas Jefferson|Thomas Jefferson was the 3rd president of the United States and the main author of the Declaration of Independence. He bought Louisiana from France in 1803. He died on 4 July 1826, fifty years after the Declaration.

bio|07-04|1826|Τζον Άνταμς|John Adams|John Adams was the 2nd president of the United States and a leading figure of the American Revolution. He died on 4 July 1826, the same day as Jefferson, fifty years after the Declaration of Independence.

bio|07-04|1831|Τζέιμς Μόνροου|James Monroe|James Monroe was the 5th president of the United States, from 1817 to 1825. His name is borne by the "Monroe Doctrine", which opposed European intervention in America. He died in 1831.

bio|07-04|1872|Κάλβιν Κούλιτζ|Calvin Coolidge|Calvin Coolidge was the 30th president of the United States, from 1923 to 1929. He was a conservative who supported the reduction of government spending. He became president after the death of Harding.

bio|07-04|1926|Αλφρέδο Ντι Στέφανο|Alfredo Di Stéfano|Alfredo Di Stéfano was born in Argentina and was one of the greatest footballers in history. He played for Real Madrid in the 1950s and won five consecutive European Cups. He died in 2014.

bio|07-04|1934|Μαρία Κιουρί|Marie Curie|Marie Curie was born in Warsaw and lived in France. She studied radioactivity and discovered polonium and radium. She won two Nobel Prizes, in Physics in 1903 and in Chemistry in 1911. She died in 1934.

bio|07-05|1820|Ουίλιαμ Ράνκιν|William Rankine|William Rankine was a Scottish engineer and physicist. He contributed to thermodynamics and to the study of steam engines, and the Rankine scale of temperature is named after him.

bio|07-05|1853|Σέσιλ Ρόουντς|Cecil Rhodes|Cecil Rhodes was a British businessman and politician in South Africa. He founded the diamond company De Beers and was prime minister of the Cape Colony. His fortune funds the Rhodes Scholarships.

bio|07-05|1889|Ζαν Κοκτώ|Jean Cocteau|Jean Cocteau was a French poet, playwright and director. He wrote the novel "Les Enfants Terribles" and directed the film "Beauty and the Beast" in 1946. He died in 1963.

bio|07-05|1911|Ζωρζ Πομπιντού|Georges Pompidou|Georges Pompidou was a French politician. He was prime minister under de Gaulle and president of France from 1969 until his death in 1974. The Pompidou Centre in Paris is named after him.

bio|07-05|1948|Ζωρζ Μπερνανός|Georges Bernanos|Georges Bernanos was a French writer with a deep Catholic faith. He wrote "Diary of a Country Priest" and "Dialogues of the Carmelites". He died in 1948.

bio|07-05|1969|Βάλτερ Γκρόπιους|Walter Gropius|Walter Gropius was a German architect and the founder of the Bauhaus, the school of art and design that began in 1919. He left Germany under the Nazi regime and taught at Harvard.

bio|07-05|1969|Λίο ΜακΚάρεϊ|Leo McCarey|Leo McCarey was an American director of comedies. He directed the Marx Brothers' "Duck Soup" and "The Awful Truth", and he won an Oscar for Best Director for "Going My Way".

bio|07-05|1975|Ότο Σκορτσένυ|Otto Skorzeny|Otto Skorzeny was an Austrian SS officer. He became known in 1943, when he led the operation that freed Mussolini from captivity in the mountains. After the war he lived in Spain.
bio|07-05|1980|Εύα Γκριν|Eva Green|Eva Green is a French actress. She became known through Bertolucci's film "The Dreamers" and played Vesper Lynd in "Casino Royale" and appeared in "Dark Shadows".

bio|07-06|1535|Τόμας Μορ|Thomas More|Thomas More was an English lawyer, writer and politician. He wrote the book "Utopia". He was Lord Chancellor of Henry VIII, but he refused to recognise the king as head of the Church, and he was beheaded in 1535.

bio|07-06|1893|Γκυ ντε Μωπασσάν|Guy de Maupassant|Guy de Maupassant was a French writer and a great master of the short story. He wrote "Boule de Suif" and the novel "Bel-Ami". In his last years he suffered from mental illness.

bio|07-06|1907|Φρίντα Κάλο|Frida Kahlo|Frida Kahlo was born in Mexico. She painted mainly self-portraits, influenced by the pain after a serious accident and by Mexican tradition. She was married to the painter Diego Rivera. She died in 1954.

bio|07-06|1935|Τενζίν Γκιάτσο|Tenzin Gyatso|Tenzin Gyatso is the 14th Dalai Lama, the spiritual leader of the Tibetans. He left Tibet in 1959 after the Chinese crackdown and lives in India. In 1989 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize.

bio|07-06|1940|Νουρσουλτάν Ναζαρμπάγιεφ|Nursultan Nazarbayev|Nursultan Nazarbayev was the first president of Kazakhstan, from independence in 1991 until 2019. He governed with strong authority, and the capital Astana was for a time named after him.
bio|07-06|1946|Σιλβέστερ Σταλόνε|Sylvester Stallone|Sylvester Stallone is an American actor and screenwriter. He became known as the boxer Rocky Balboa, a role that he wrote himself, and as Rambo.

bio|07-06|1962|Γουίλιαμ Φώκνερ|William Faulkner|William Faulkner was an American writer from the American South. He wrote "The Sound and the Fury" and "As I Lay Dying". In 1949 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1962.

bio|07-06|1971|Λούις Άρμστρονγκ|Louis Armstrong|Louis Armstrong was an American jazz trumpeter and singer with a characteristic gravelly voice. He grew up in New Orleans and recorded hits such as "What a Wonderful World". He died in 1971.
bio|07-06|1975|50 Cent|50 Cent|50 Cent, real name Curtis Jackson, is an American rapper and businessman from Queens, New York. He became known with the album "Get Rich or Die Tryin'" in 2003.

bio|07-07|1307|Εδουάρδος Α΄|Edward I|Edward I was king of England from 1272. He conquered Wales and fought the Scots, and he was given the nickname "Hammer of the Scots". He died in 1307 on his way to Scotland.

bio|07-07|1843|Καμίλλο Γκόλτζι|Camillo Golgi|Camillo Golgi was an Italian doctor and histologist. He developed a method for staining nerve cells and described the Golgi apparatus. In 1906 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Ramón y Cajal.

bio|07-07|1860|Γκούσταβ Μάλερ|Gustav Mahler|Gustav Mahler was an Austrian composer and conductor. He wrote nine completed symphonies and songs for voice and orchestra, including "Das Lied von der Erde". He directed the Vienna Opera. He died in 1911.

bio|07-07|1887|Μαρκ Σαγκάλ|Marc Chagall|Marc Chagall was born in Belarus and lived in France. He was a painter with a dreamlike style, with vivid colours and floating figures. He also painted the ceiling of the Paris Opera.

bio|07-07|1901|Βιττόριο ντε Σίκα|Vittorio De Sica|Vittorio De Sica was an Italian director and actor of Italian neorealism. He directed "The Bicycle Thief" and "Umberto D.", and he also acted in films himself.

bio|07-07|1930|Άρθουρ Κόναν Ντόυλ|Arthur Conan Doyle|Arthur Conan Doyle was a Scottish writer and doctor. He created the detective Sherlock Holmes and Doctor Watson. He also wrote historical novels and was involved in spiritualism. He died in 1930.

bio|07-07|1940|Ρίνγκο Σταρ|Ringo Starr|Ringo Starr, real name Richard Starkey, was born in Liverpool and was the drummer of the Beatles. He also sang on some of their songs, such as "Yellow Submarine". He continues to have a solo career.

bio|07-07|2014|Έντβαρντ Σεβαρντνάτζε|Eduard Shevardnadze|Eduard Shevardnadze was a Georgian politician. He was foreign minister of the Soviet Union under Gorbachev and later president of Georgia, from 1995 to 2003, when he resigned after the Rose Revolution.

bio|07-07|2014|Αλφρέδο Ντι Στέφανο|Alfredo Di Stéfano|Alfredo Di Stéfano died in Madrid in 2014. He was an Argentine footballer and later a coach. He was a star of Real Madrid, who won five European Cups, and he is regarded as one of the greatest of his era.

bio|07-08|1593|Αρτεμίζια Τζεντιλέσκι|Artemisia Gentileschi|Artemisia Gentileschi was an Italian Baroque painter. She painted powerful female figures, such as "Judith Slaying Holofernes". She managed to be accepted into the Academy of Drawing in Florence.

bio|07-08|1621|Ζαν ντε Λα Φονταίν|Jean de La Fontaine|Jean de La Fontaine was a French writer. He became known for his "Fables", poetic adaptations of the fables of Aesop and other sources, which are taught in many schools. He died in 1695.

bio|07-08|1695|Κρίστιαν Χόυχενς|Christiaan Huygens|Christiaan Huygens was a Dutch physicist and astronomer. He discovered Titan, a moon of Saturn, and the shape of its rings, and he built the pendulum clock. He also formulated the wave theory of light.

bio|07-08|1822|Πέρσι Σέλλεϋ|Percy Bysshe Shelley|Percy Bysshe Shelley was an English Romantic poet. He wrote "Prometheus Unbound" and "Ozymandias", and he was a philhellene: his drama "Hellas" was inspired by the Greek revolution. He drowned in Italy at the age of 29.

bio|07-08|1839|Τζον Ντ. Ροκφέλερ|John D. Rockefeller|John D. Rockefeller was an American businessman. He founded Standard Oil and became one of the richest people in history. Later he donated large sums for charitable purposes.

bio|07-08|1894|Πιοτρ Καπίτσα|Pyotr Kapitsa|Pyotr Kapitsa was a Russian physicist. He studied very low temperatures and discovered the superfluidity of helium. In 1978 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|07-08|1967|Βίβιαν Λι|Vivien Leigh|Vivien Leigh was an English actress. She won an Oscar for playing Scarlett O'Hara in "Gone with the Wind" and for playing Blanche in "A Streetcar Named Desire". She died in 1967, at the age of 53.
bio|07-08|1992|Σον Χιουνγκ-μιν|Son Heung-min|Son Heung-min is a South Korean footballer, a forward. He played for Tottenham and is the captain of the South Korean national team.

bio|07-08|1994|Κιμ Ίλ-σονγκ|Kim Il-sung|Kim Il-sung was the founder and first leader of North Korea, from 1948 until his death in 1994. He created a regime built on a cult of personality, and he was succeeded by his son Kim Jong-il.

bio|07-09|1441|Γιαν βαν Άικ|Jan van Eyck|Jan van Eyck was a Flemish painter. He is regarded as a pioneer of oil painting, with works such as the "Arnolfini Portrait" and the "Ghent Altarpiece", which he painted together with his brother Hubert.

bio|07-09|1797|Έντμουντ Μπερκ|Edmund Burke|Edmund Burke was an Irish politician and thinker and a member of the British Parliament. In "Reflections on the Revolution in France" he criticised the French Revolution and he is regarded as the founder of modern conservatism.
bio|07-09|1819|Έλιας Χάου|Elias Howe|Elias Howe was an American inventor. In 1846 he patented a sewing machine with two threads, which was later improved by others, such as Isaac Singer.

bio|07-09|1850|Ζαχαρίας Τέιλορ|Zachary Taylor|Zachary Taylor was the 12th president of the United States. He was a general who became a hero of the Mexican War. He died in 1850, after 16 months in office.

bio|07-09|1856|Αμεντέο Αβογκάντρο|Amedeo Avogadro|Amedeo Avogadro was an Italian physicist and chemist. He put forward the hypothesis that equal volumes of gases contain the same number of molecules. Avogadro's number is named after him.

bio|07-09|1950|Βίκτορ Γιανουκόβιτς|Viktor Yanukovych|Viktor Yanukovych is a Ukrainian politician. He was prime minister and from 2010 president of Ukraine, until 2014, when his decision not to sign an agreement with the European Union caused large protests and he was overthrown.

bio|07-09|1956|Τομ Χανκς|Tom Hanks|Tom Hanks is an American actor. He won two consecutive Oscars, for "Philadelphia" and "Forrest Gump", and he appeared in "Saving Private Ryan", "The Green Mile" and "Cast Away".
bio|07-09|1964|Κόρτνεϊ Λαβ|Courtney Love|Courtney Love is an American singer and actress. She was the leader of the rock band Hole and was married to Kurt Cobain of Nirvana.

bio|07-09|1966|Αμελί Νοτόμπ|Amélie Nothomb|Amélie Nothomb is a Belgian writer who writes in French. She wrote novels such as "The Hygiene of the Assassin" and "Fear and Trembling". She was born in Japan, and her experiences inspire many of her works.

bio|07-10|138|Αδριανός|Hadrian|Hadrian was Roman emperor from 117 to 138. He visited many provinces, built Hadrian's Wall in Britain and loved Greece, especially Athens, where he completed the Olympieion and built the Library of Hadrian.

bio|07-10|1099|Ελ Σιντ|El Cid|El Cid, real name Rodrigo Díaz de Vivar, was a Spanish knight. He served both Christian and Muslim rulers and took Valencia in 1094. He became a hero of Spanish tradition.

bio|07-10|1509|Ιωάννης Καλβίνος|John Calvin|John Calvin was born in France and was a theologian of the Reformation. He lived and taught in Geneva, and his work "Institutes of the Christian Religion" established Calvinism. He died in 1564.

bio|07-10|1584|Γουλιέλμος Α΄|William I of Orange|William I of Orange, "the Silent", was the leader of the revolt of the Low Countries against Spain. He was assassinated in 1584 in Delft and is regarded as the father of the Netherlands.

bio|07-10|1830|Καμίλ Πισαρό|Camille Pissarro|Camille Pissarro was a French painter and one of the pioneers of Impressionism. He was born in the Virgin Islands and painted landscapes and scenes of Paris. He took part in all the Impressionist exhibitions.

bio|07-10|1856|Νίκολα Τέσλα|Nikola Tesla|Nikola Tesla was born in Croatia to Serbian parents and emigrated to the United States. He was an inventor and electrical engineer. He contributed to the development of alternating current and invented the Tesla coil. He died in 1943.
bio|07-10|1871|Μαρσέλ Προυστ|Marcel Proust|Marcel Proust was a French writer. He wrote the seven-volume novel "In Search of Lost Time", about memory and the society of his time. He died in 1922.

bio|07-10|1925|Μαχαθίρ Μοχάμαντ|Mahathir Mohamad|Mahathir Mohamad is a Malaysian politician. He was prime minister of Malaysia from 1981 to 2003 and again from 2018 to 2020, which made him the oldest head of government in the world.

bio|07-10|2015|Ομάρ Σαρίφ|Omar Sharif|Omar Sharif was an Egyptian actor. He became famous in the West with the films "Lawrence of Arabia" and "Doctor Zhivago". He was also a leading bridge player. He died in 2015.

bio|07-11|1274|Ροβέρτος Α΄|Robert I|Robert I the Bruce was king of Scotland from 1306 to 1329. He led the war of independence against England and defeated the English in 1314 at the Battle of Bannockburn.

bio|07-11|1593|Τζουζέπε Αρτσιμπόλντο|Giuseppe Arcimboldo|Giuseppe Arcimboldo was an Italian painter. He became known for his portraits that are composed of faces made of fruit, vegetables, flowers and other objects. He worked at the court of the Habsburgs.

bio|07-11|1767|Τζον Κουίνσι Άνταμς|John Quincy Adams|John Quincy Adams was the 6th president of the United States, from 1825 to 1829, and the son of John Adams. He had a significant career as a diplomat and later became a member of Congress, where he opposed slavery.

bio|07-11|1916|Αλεξάντρ Πρόχοροφ|Aleksandr Prokhorov|Aleksandr Prokhorov was a Russian physicist. He contributed to the development of lasers and masers, and in 1964 he shared the Nobel Prize in Physics with Basov and Townes.

bio|07-11|1920|Γιουλ Μπρίνερ|Yul Brynner|Yul Brynner was born in Russia and became an American actor, known for his shaved head. He won an Oscar for the role of the king in "The King and I" and appeared in "The Magnificent Seven".

bio|07-11|1934|Τζόρτζιο Αρμάνι|Giorgio Armani|Giorgio Armani is an Italian fashion designer. He founded the fashion house bearing his name in 1975 and became known for elegant, flexible menswear and womenswear.

bio|07-11|1937|Τζορτζ Γκέρσουιν|George Gershwin|George Gershwin was an American composer. He combined classical music and jazz in works such as "Rhapsody in Blue" and "An American in Paris", and he wrote the opera "Porgy and Bess". He died young, at the age of 38.

bio|07-11|1974|Παίρ Λάγκερκβιστ|Pär Lagerkvist|Pär Lagerkvist was a Swedish writer. He wrote the novel "Barabbas" and other works that deal with good and evil. In 1951 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1974.

bio|07-11|1989|Λόρενς Ολίβιε|Laurence Olivier|Laurence Olivier was an English actor and director and a leading interpreter of Shakespeare. He starred in and directed "Hamlet" in 1948, which won him an Oscar, and he was the first director of Britain's National Theatre. He died in 1989.

bio|07-12|-100|Γάιος Ιούλιος Καίσαρας|Julius Caesar|Gaius Julius Caesar was a Roman general and politician. He conquered Gaul, defeated Pompey in the civil war and became dictator. He was assassinated in 44 BC. The date of his birth is uncertain, and 12 July comes from tradition.

bio|07-12|1536|Έρασμος|Erasmus|Erasmus of Rotterdam was a Dutch humanist and theologian. He wrote "In Praise of Folly" and published the first printed edition of the New Testament in Greek. He died in Basel in 1536.

bio|07-12|1712|Ρίτσαρντ Κρόμγουελ|Richard Cromwell|Richard Cromwell was the son of Oliver Cromwell and succeeded him as Lord Protector of England in 1658. He resigned in 1659, and in 1660 the monarchy was restored. He lived abroad for several years.

bio|07-12|1804|Αλεξάντερ Χάμιλτον|Alexander Hamilton|Alexander Hamilton was an American politician and the first Secretary of the Treasury of the United States. He was one of the authors of "The Federalist Papers". He was mortally wounded in a duel with Aaron Burr in 1804.

bio|07-12|1895|Ρίτσαρντ Μπάκμινστερ Φούλερ|Buckminster Fuller|Buckminster Fuller was an American architect, engineer and writer. He became known for the geodesic dome and the phrase "spaceship Earth". He died in 1983.

bio|07-12|1904|Πάμπλο Νερούδα|Pablo Neruda|Pablo Neruda was a Chilean poet and diplomat. He wrote "Twenty Love Poems and a Song of Despair" and "Canto General". In 1971 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He died in 1973.

bio|07-12|1921|Γκαμπριέλ Λιπμάν|Gabriel Lippmann|Gabriel Lippmann was a French physicist. He devised a method of colour photography based on the interference of light, and in 1908 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Physics.

bio|07-12|1991|Χάμες Ροδρίγες|James Rodríguez|James Rodríguez is a Colombian footballer, an attacking midfielder. He became the top scorer at the 2014 World Cup, and he has played for Real Madrid and Bayern Munich.

bio|07-12|1997|Μαλάλα Γιουσαφζάι|Malala Yousafzai|Malala Yousafzai was born in Pakistan and campaigns for girls' right to education. In 2012 she was shot by the Taliban and survived. In 2014 she became the youngest winner of the Nobel Peace Prize, at the age of 17.

bio|07-13|1793|Ζαν Πολ Μαρά|Jean-Paul Marat|Jean-Paul Marat was a French doctor, journalist and leading figure of the French Revolution. He was stabbed in his bath in 1793 by Charlotte Corday, and his death was depicted in a famous painting by David.

bio|07-13|1927|Σιμόν Βέιλ|Simone Veil|Simone Veil was born in Nice in 1927. She survived Auschwitz and later became France's minister of health and the first president of the European Parliament. She became known for the 1975 law that legalised abortion.

bio|07-13|1934|Γουόλε Σογίνκα|Wole Soyinka|Wole Soyinka is a Nigerian playwright and poet. In 1986 he became the first African to be awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. He criticised the military regimes of his country.

bio|07-13|1940|Πάτρικ Στιούαρτ|Patrick Stewart|Patrick Stewart is an English actor. He became known as Captain Jean-Luc Picard in "Star Trek" and as Professor Xavier in the "X-Men" films. He has also performed a great deal on stage, mainly in Shakespeare.
bio|07-13|1942|Χάρισον Φορντ|Harrison Ford|Harrison Ford is an American actor. He became famous as Han Solo in "Star Wars" and as Indiana Jones, and he appeared in "Blade Runner" and "Witness".
bio|07-13|1950|Μα Γινγκ-Τζέου|Ma Ying-jeou|Ma Ying-jeou is a Taiwanese politician. He was president of Taiwan from 2008 to 2016 and promoted better relations with mainland China.

bio|07-13|1954|Φρίντα Κάλο|Frida Kahlo|Frida Kahlo died in 1954 in her house in Mexico City, in the so-called "Blue House". She was a Mexican painter, known for her self-portraits, and today she is an image of Mexican identity.

bio|07-13|2014|Ναντίν Γκόρντιμερ|Nadine Gordimer|Nadine Gordimer was a South African writer. In her works she described the consequences of apartheid. In 1991 she was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature. She died in 2014.

bio|07-13|2017|Λιου Σιαομπό|Liu Xiaobo|Liu Xiaobo was a Chinese writer and activist for democracy. He co-wrote "Charter 08" and was imprisoned. In 2010 he was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize, and he died in 2017 while in custody.

bio|07-14|1223|Φίλιππος Β΄|Philip II of France|Philip II Augustus was king of France from 1180 to 1223. He greatly expanded the territory of the kingdom, taking Normandy from the king of England. He took part in the Third Crusade.

bio|07-14|1743|Γαβριήλ Ντερζάβιν|Gavrila Derzhavin|Gavrila Derzhavin was a Russian poet and politician of the 18th century. He wrote the ode "Felitsa" for Catherine the Great, and he is regarded as one of the great poets before Pushkin.

bio|07-14|1827|Αυγουστίνος Φρενέλ|Augustin-Jean Fresnel|Augustin-Jean Fresnel was a French physicist and engineer. He argued for the wave nature of light and invented the Fresnel lens, which is used in lighthouses. He died young, at the age of 39.

bio|07-14|1862|Γκούσταβ Κλιμτ|Gustav Klimt|Gustav Klimt was an Austrian painter of Symbolism and the founder of the Vienna Secession. He painted "The Kiss" and "Adele Bloch-Bauer I", with golden decorative elements. He died in 1918.

bio|07-14|1913|Τζέραλντ Φορντ|Gerald Ford|Gerald Ford was the 38th president of the United States. He became president in 1974 after Nixon's resignation, without having been elected to the office, and he pardoned him. He died in 2006.

bio|07-14|1918|Ίνγκμαρ Μπέργκμαν|Ingmar Bergman|Ingmar Bergman was a Swedish director. He directed "The Seventh Seal", "Wild Strawberries" and "Fanny and Alexander", with themes such as death, faith and human relationships. He died in 2007.

bio|07-14|1954|Χαθίντο Μπεναβέντε|Jacinto Benavente|Jacinto Benavente was a Spanish playwright. He wrote more than a hundred plays, with witty comedy and criticism of the middle class. In 1922 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature.
bio|07-14|1988|Κόνορ ΜακΓκρέγκορ|Conor McGregor|Conor McGregor is an Irish mixed martial arts fighter. He became UFC champion in two weight divisions and became known for his fiery personality.

bio|07-14|2017|Μαριάμ Μιρζαχανί|Maryam Mirzakhani|Maryam Mirzakhani was an Iranian mathematician and professor at Stanford University. In 2014 she became the first woman to be awarded the Fields Medal. She died of cancer in 2017, at the age of 40.

bio|07-15|1015|Βλαδίμηρος Α΄|Vladimir I of Kiev|Vladimir I was grand prince of Kiev. Around 988 he was baptised a Christian and established Christianity as the official religion of Kievan Rus, in close relations with Byzantium. The Russian Church honours him as a saint.

bio|07-15|1606|Ρέμπραντ|Rembrandt|Rembrandt van Rijn was a Dutch painter of the Golden Age. He became known for his portraits and self-portraits and for his play of light and shadow, with works such as "The Night Watch". He died in 1669.

bio|07-15|1892|Βάλτερ Μπένγιαμιν|Walter Benjamin|Walter Benjamin was a German-Jewish critic and philosopher. He wrote the essay "The Work of Art in the Age of Its Technological Reproducibility". He took his own life in 1940 on the French-Spanish border, while fleeing the Nazis.

bio|07-15|1904|Αντόν Τσέχωφ|Anton Chekhov|Anton Chekhov was a Russian writer and doctor. He wrote many short stories and the plays "The Seagull", "Uncle Vanya", "Three Sisters" and "The Cherry Orchard". He died of tuberculosis in 1904.
bio|07-15|1919|Εμίλ Φίσερ|Emil Fischer|Emil Fischer was a German chemist. He studied the structure of sugars and proteins, and in 1902 he was awarded the Nobel Prize in Chemistry. He died in 1919.

bio|07-15|1930|Ζακ Ντεριντά|Jacques Derrida|Jacques Derrida was born in Algeria and was a French philosopher. He developed "deconstruction", a method of reading texts, which had a great influence on philosophy and literary theory. He died in 2004.

bio|07-15|1939|Αλί Χαμενεΐ|Ali Khamenei|Ali Khamenei is an Iranian religious and political leader. He was president of Iran from 1981 to 1989, and after Khomeini he succeeded him as Supreme Leader of the country.
